summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with a flare. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control using IV hydromorphone, which was later transitioned to oral medications. A chest X-ray and fluoroscopic evaluation confirmed the PICC line was in satisfactory position for TPN, so no repositioning was needed. The pain service recommended increasing gabapentin, which was initiated at 600 mg nightly with a plan for outpatient uptitration. She gradually improved, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with TPN, a stable PICC line, and follow-up plans with her gastroenterologist for medication management and nutritional support.
